newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA CURRENT ACCOUNT-Review of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA CURRENT ACCOUNT-Review of forecasts.

text.p: Australia's July current account deficit will be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.
Economists' median forecast is for a deficit of A$1.3 billion, essentially unchanged from June's A$1.291 billion.
Forecasts of the 27 economists Reuters surveyed ranged from A$1.1 to A$1.6 billion, with the already published 2.8 percent fall in July exports a key to the relatively low forecasts.

Economists said that while a fall in exports was likely after the strong 4.1 percent rise seen in June, they were still expected to come in above imports, meaning Australia will post consecutive monthly trade surpluses for the first time since January and February 1994.
Exports would have to fall by over 4.9 percent for the trade balance to fall back into deficit, an event economists see as unlikely.

The incorporation of the June quarter survey of foreign investment into the data will see some revisions. After the release of June quarter balance of payments data on Tuesday, economists said it appeared the net income deficit for the June quarter would fall by around A$243 million.
In turn, this would produce a lower starting point for the July net income deficit, which would increase the downside risks of the current account deficit forecasts, they said.

The government forecast for the 1996/97 current account deficit of A$20 billion, or four percent of GDP, indicated no substantial improvement was expected over the coming year from the 1995/96 result of just over A$20 billion, or just over four percent of GDP.

This highlighted the long term nature of the current account deficit, and the floor the net income deficit places under it, economists said, and reinforced the need for the budget to be moved into, and sustained in, surplus.
